question: What are the differences in thermal relaxation rates and activation energies of naphthopyran molecules in anisotropic versus isotropic phases of mesogenic solvents?
answer: Naphthopyran thermal relaxation rates are slower in ordered mesogenic solvents (5CB, 8CB) compared to isotropic solvents (toluene) and increase with temperature following Arrhenius behavior.  Activation energies for relaxation are higher in the ordered phases of liquid crystals, indicating the influence of solvent order and viscosity on the ring-closure process.

The purpose of the paper is to investigate the thermal relaxation behavior of naphthopyran photoproducts in guest-host liquid crystal (LC) mixtures, specifically focusing on how temperature and excitation conditions influence relaxation rates in anisotropic (ordered) and isotropic (disordered) states of mesogenic solvents. The study aims to understand how the organization of the liquid crystal host environment affects the activation energy and relaxation dynamics of the guest naphthopyran species.
